text: Left side of the whistle is missing radii. Add radii to the edges of the bigger part of the whistle. Radii must be same as the ones on the other side

Let's make this part symmetric. There is a step on one of the sides of the whistle. Move the protruding surface so that it is level with the surface next to it. Delete all chamfers and radii and new ones following rules: Horizontal edges in the area where the narrow and bigger part of the whistle meet have a radius R=20mm. Other edges have R=5mm applied to them

Add circular feature that will act as a attachment for hanging rope. Outer D=4cm and feature has a concentric hole D=2cm. Thickness is 3cm. Feature is touching tangentially vertical surface of the bigger feature of the whistle with its hole and axis is parallel to this surface. Try to centre the feature to the aforementioned surface

If this is a spanner, the main cutout is too deep which is weakening the tool. Make the cutout shallower by 10mm, but keep the "size" of the spanner the same - meaning the parallel surfaces remain 20mm apart.

Make the part symmetrical with respect to ZX plane by adding lowered plateau to the bottom. Then add embossed text to the top to distinguish the top (text should be "TOP", Arial, 10mm height, 1mm raised above lowered plateau, not sticking out of the plateau, approximately centered to the middle).
Use geometry of cylindrical hole defined in Sketch4 for creating inscribed hexagonal polygonal to the original hole and make it through all cutout instead.
Mirror the part according to the plane lying on the not rounded end of the part. Merge the mirrored part together with the existing one so they create one body.
Multiply amount of cylindrical feature to 4. Imagine this is a system of plant pots, so you need to add stability to that afterwards by adding another legs or ribs on the sides.
Design cylindrical bearing on the flat end of the part (the one without fillet). Create another 7 instances of this design and rotate them around the bearing axis.
